questions.korean: 그건 양날의 검이야.
answers: That's a double-edged sword.
It cuts both ways.
questions.hint: double-edged sword / cut both ways = 양날의 검

questions.korean: 그들은 큰 그림을 놓치고 있어.
answers: They're missing the forest for the trees.
They're losing sight of the bigger picture.
questions.hint: miss the forest for the trees = 큰 그림을 보지 못하다

questions.korean: 그게 밝혀졌을 때, 판도라의 상자가 열렸어.
answers: When it came out, it opened a can of worms.
That revelation opened Pandora's box.
questions.hint: open a can of worms = 복잡한 문제를 일으키다
questions.explanation: open Pandora's box = 판도라의 상자를 열다

questions.korean: 그건 완전히 새로운 차원의 도전이야.
answers: That's a whole different ball game.
That takes things to a whole new level.
questions.hint: a whole different ball game = 완전히 다른 차원

questions.korean: 우리는 같은 배를 타고 있어.
answers: We're all in the same boat.
We're going through the same thing together.
questions.hint: in the same boat = 같은 처지에 있다

questions.korean: 그건 순환 논리야.
answers: That's circular reasoning.
That argument is going in circles.
questions.hint: circular reasoning / going in circles = 순환 논리

questions.korean: 그건 핵심을 벗어난 주장이야.
answers: That's beside the point.
That argument misses the mark.
questions.hint: beside the point / misses the mark = 핵심을 벗어나다

questions.korean: 그건 더 생각해볼 여지가 있어.
answers: That deserves further consideration.
There's room to think that through more carefully.
questions.hint: deserves further consideration / room to think through

questions.korean: 그 주장은 설득력이 있어.
answers: That's a compelling argument.
The logic behind that is sound.
questions.hint: compelling / sound logic = 설득력 있는, 논리가 탄탄한

questions.korean: 그게 선례가 될 수 있어.
answers: That could set a precedent.
That might establish a standard for future cases.
questions.hint: set a precedent = 선례를 남기다

questions.korean: 큰 그림을 보면서 세부 사항도 챙겨야 해.
answers: You need to see the big picture while managing the details.
Keep an eye on the horizon without losing track of the specifics.
questions.hint: big picture + manage the details = 큰 그림과 세부 사항

questions.korean: 팀원들의 강점을 최대한 활용해야 해.
answers: You need to leverage the strengths of your team members.
Make the most of what each team member brings to the table.
questions.hint: leverage strengths / make the most of = 강점을 활용하다

questions.korean: 그는 압박 속에서도 침착함을 유지해.
answers: He remains composed under pressure.
He keeps his cool even in high-pressure situations.
questions.hint: remain composed / keep one's cool = 침착함을 유지하다

questions.korean: 우리는 목표를 향해 한 방향으로 나아가야 해.
answers: We need to align ourselves toward a common goal.
We have to move in the same direction to achieve our objectives.
questions.hint: align toward / move in the same direction = 한 방향으로

questions.korean: 그는 팀에게 영감을 줬어.
answers: He inspired the team.
He brought out the best in everyone.
questions.hint: inspire / bring out the best in = 영감을 주다
questions.explanation: bring out the best in = ~의 최선을 이끌어내다

questions.korean: 아이러니하게도, 그 해결책이 더 큰 문제를 일으켰어.
answers: Ironically, the solution created a bigger problem.
As ironic as it sounds, the fix made things worse.
questions.hint: ironically / as ironic as it sounds = 아이러니하게도

questions.korean: 더 많이 가질수록 더 많이 원하게 돼.
answers: The more you have, the more you want.
Having more only makes you crave more.
questions.hint: the more ~ the more = ~할수록 더 ~하다

questions.korean: 그건 의도하지 않은 결과야.
answers: That's an unintended consequence.
That's a case of the law of unintended effects.
questions.hint: unintended consequence = 의도하지 않은 결과

questions.korean: 역설적으로, 더 적게 일하면 더 생산적이 될 수도 있어.
answers: Paradoxically, working less can make you more productive.
It's a paradox, but less work sometimes leads to more output.
questions.hint: paradoxically / it's a paradox = 역설적으로

questions.korean: 자유를 얻기 위해 규칙을 따라야 할 때도 있어.
answers: Sometimes you have to follow the rules in order to be truly free.
There's a certain irony in needing discipline to achieve freedom.
questions.hint: there's a certain irony in = ~에는 아이러니가 있다

questions.korean: 그 사건이 일어나기 훨씬 전부터 문제는 있었어.
answers: Long before the incident occurred, the problem was already there.
The issues predated the incident by a significant margin.
questions.hint: long before / predate = 훨씬 전부터

questions.korean: 결국 돌아보면, 그게 전환점이었어.
answers: Looking back, that turned out to be the turning point.
In hindsight, that was the pivotal moment.
questions.hint: in hindsight / looking back = 돌아보면, turning point = 전환점

questions.korean: 그 변화는 서서히 일어났지만 지속적이었어.
answers: The change happened gradually but persistently.
It was a slow but steady transformation.
questions.hint: gradually but persistently / slow but steady

questions.korean: 지금 이 시점에서, 모든 선택지가 다 열려 있어.
answers: At this juncture, all options are still on the table.
Right now, every avenue remains open.
questions.hint: at this juncture = 이 시점에서, options on the table = 선택지가 열려 있다

questions.korean: 그게 역사의 흐름을 바꿨어.
answers: It changed the course of history.
That altered the trajectory of history.
questions.hint: change the course of / alter the trajectory = 흐름을 바꾸다

questions.korean: 두 접근 방식 모두 장단점이 있어.
answers: Both approaches have their merits and drawbacks.
Each method comes with its own advantages and disadvantages.
questions.hint: merits and drawbacks / advantages and disadvantages = 장단점

questions.korean: 이 두 방식의 가장 큰 차이는 비용이야.
answers: The key distinction between the two is the cost.
What sets them apart most is the price difference.
questions.hint: key distinction / what sets them apart = 가장 큰 차이

questions.korean: 첫 번째 옵션은 위험하지만 더 빠르고, 두 번째는 더 안전하지만 느려.
answers: The first option is riskier but faster, while the second is safer but slower.
Option one carries more risk but offers greater speed; option two is safer at the cost of efficiency.
questions.hint: riskier but faster / safer but slower = 위험하지만 빠른 vs. 안전하지만 느린

questions.korean: 어떤 면에서는 비슷하지만, 근본적으로는 달라.
answers: They are similar in some ways, but fundamentally different.
On the surface they look alike, but deep down they're quite different.
questions.hint: similar in some ways / fundamentally different

questions.korean: 두 방식을 비교해보면, 두 번째가 훨씬 효율적이야.
answers: Comparing the two, the second is far more efficient.
When you put them side by side, the second clearly outperforms the first.
questions.hint: comparing the two / side by side = 비교해보면

questions.korean: 그 제안을 수락하기로 했어.
answers: I've decided to accept the proposal.
I'm going to go ahead with the offer.
questions.hint: decided to accept (격식) / go ahead with (구어)

questions.korean: 그는 그것을 성공적으로 완수했어.
answers: He successfully completed the task.
He pulled it off without a hitch.
questions.hint: successfully completed (격식) / pulled it off (구어)

questions.korean: 그 정보는 신뢰할 수 없어.
answers: The information is unreliable.
You can't trust that information.
questions.hint: unreliable (격식) / can't trust (구어)

questions.korean: 그 주장은 근거가 부족해.
answers: The argument lacks substantiation.
That claim doesn't hold up.
questions.hint: lacks substantiation (격식) / doesn't hold up (구어)

questions.korean: 나는 그 문제에 대해 깊이 고민해봤어.
answers: I gave the matter considerable thought.
I've been chewing on that problem for a while.
questions.hint: gave considerable thought (격식) / chewing on (구어)

questions.korean: 우리는 모두 같은 목표를 향해 일해야 해.
answers: We all need to be working toward the same goal.
Everyone has to pull in the same direction.
questions.hint: pull in the same direction = 같은 방향으로 힘을 모으다

questions.korean: 그것은 모두의 공동 노력의 결과야.
answers: It's the result of a collective effort.
It took a team effort to make this happen.
questions.hint: collective effort / team effort = 공동 노력

questions.korean: 역할 분담이 명확해야 해.
answers: The division of roles needs to be clear.
Everyone should know their responsibilities.
questions.hint: division of roles / responsibilities = 역할 분담

questions.korean: 우리는 각자의 전문성을 활용해야 해.
answers: We should leverage each person's expertise.
We need to tap into everyone's strengths.
questions.hint: leverage expertise / tap into strengths = 전문성을 활용하다

questions.korean: 소통의 부재가 가장 큰 문제야.
answers: The lack of communication is the biggest issue.
A breakdown in communication is at the root of the problem.
questions.hint: lack of communication / breakdown in communication

questions.korean: 만약 처음부터 계획이 있었다면 이 지경이 되지 않았을 거야.
answers: Had there been a plan from the start, it wouldn't have come to this.
If a plan had been in place from the beginning, we wouldn't be in this situation.
questions.hint: Had there been = If there had been (도치)

questions.korean: 설령 그게 사실이라 해도, 변명은 되지 않아.
answers: Even assuming that's true, it's no excuse.
Even if that were the case, it wouldn't justify anything.
questions.hint: even assuming / even if that were the case = 설령 ~이라 해도

questions.korean: 그게 어떻게 됐든, 우리는 계속 전진해야 해.
answers: Whatever the outcome, we have to keep moving forward.
Regardless of how it turns out, we must press on.
questions.hint: whatever the outcome / regardless of how = 어떻게 됐든

questions.korean: 이런 상황이 아니었다면, 우리는 다른 선택을 했을 거야.
answers: Were it not for these circumstances, we would have made a different choice.
In the absence of these conditions, we would have chosen differently.
questions.hint: Were it not for = If it were not for (도치)

questions.korean: 우리가 더 빠르게 움직였더라면, 그 기회를 잡을 수 있었을 거야.
answers: Had we acted more swiftly, we could have seized the opportunity.
If we had moved faster, we would have been able to capitalize on that chance.
questions.hint: had we acted more swiftly = if we had acted faster

questions.korean: 돌이켜보면, 그것이 우리가 했던 것 중 가장 훌륭한 결정이었어.
answers: In hindsight, it was the single best decision we ever made.
Looking back on it, that stands out as our finest call.
questions.hint: in hindsight / looking back = 돌이켜보면

questions.korean: 아이러니하게도, 그를 막으려던 노력이 오히려 그를 더 강하게 만들었어.
answers: Ironically, the efforts to stop him only made him stronger.
As it turned out, trying to hold him back had the opposite effect.
questions.hint: ironically / had the opposite effect = 아이러니하게도 반대 결과를 낳다

questions.korean: 그게 양날의 검인 것이 사실이야 - 우리에게 기회이기도 하지만 위험이기도 해.
answers: It's true that it's a double-edged sword — an opportunity as much as a risk.
It cuts both ways — it's as much a risk as it is an opportunity.
questions.hint: double-edged sword / cuts both ways = 양날의 검

questions.korean: 갈수록 복잡해지는 세상에서, 큰 그림을 보는 능력이 더욱 중요해지고 있어.
answers: In an increasingly complex world, the ability to see the big picture is becoming more important.
As the world grows more complicated, seeing the broader picture matters more than ever.
questions.hint: increasingly complex / grows more complicated + big picture

questions.korean: 그런 상황에서도, 그들은 침착함을 유지하고 공통점을 찾았어.
answers: Even in that situation, they remained composed and found common ground.
Despite the circumstances, they kept their cool and reached a middle ground.
questions.hint: remained composed / kept their cool + found common ground
